title: In one EM-imaged mouse retina, dendrite depth sets the ON/OFF balance of ganglion cells across types and inside mixed-polarity types, but does not set response sustainedness
abstract: Question: does the depth at which a retinal ganglion cell puts its dendrites in the inner plexiform layer (IPL) predict its visual response, and does this rule also hold for cells inside one type? Data: Eyewire Museum (Bae et al. 2018), one patch of one mouse retina with electron-microscopy stratification profiles and calcium responses to a moving bar for the same cells: 315 ganglion cells with responses in 47 types, plus 462 bipolar and 183 starburst profiles as depth landmarks. We hashed the analysis plan before we computed any structure-response statistic. Results: (1) Leave-one-type-out ridge regression from the stratification profile predicted the ON/OFF polarity index of unseen types (r = 0.63, 95% type-bootstrap interval 0.48 to 0.75, R2 = 0.36; bipolar-type overlaps r = 0.67, R2 = 0.44). (2) Inside types, cells with more inner-IPL arbor than their type mean were more ON-biased (pooled within-type r = 0.24, 0.13 to 0.36; permutation p < 0.001 after Holm correction). The within-type slope equalled the slope across type means (ratio 1.09, 0.54 to 1.69). The effect was in mixed-polarity types (r = 0.31, 15 of 18 types positive) and absent in strong-polarity types (r = 0.05). Baseline noise gave about 8% of the within-type polarity variance. (3) Stratification did not predict sustainedness of unseen types (R2 = -0.03). The central-transient / marginal-sustained rule failed across type means (Spearman 0.05) and inside types (r = -0.04); only inner-marginal cells were more sustained, as Bae et al. reported. (4) Starburst co-stratification tracked direction selectivity across type means (r = 0.68) but not inside types (r = 0.05). Limitations: one retina, one stimulus, slow calcium signal, inferred 0.125 s sample period, noisy sustainedness metric, observational data, museum type labels that partly come from stratification. Raw data are not bundled because no reuse license is stated; a retrieval script is included.
